newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends up on Japanese demand despite CBOT.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends up on Japanese demand despite CBOT.

text.p: WCE canola ended higher on heavy spread activity and late Japanese demand despite a late reversal to lower levels in CBOT soy products, traders said.

"Japan bought 150 January MOC (market on close) so we stayed up even though the reversal in Chicago weighed on us," a trader said. "About 1,500 Jan-March spread at $1," a trader said. Jan-Mar spread at $1, then $1.70. January futures crush margin fell to -38.99 from -38.11 Tuesday on January soyoil, meal. Volume was heavy at 6,305 lots, or 126,100 tonnes.
Japan bought 1,000-2,000 tonnes overnight, sources said.
January canola closed $0.70 higher at $406.40, March ended up $0.90 to $407.70.
January flax settled $1.50 higher at $357.50 on commercial demand. Jan-Mar spread at $4.50. Volume was 610 lots.

December feed wheat rose $5 to $175 as Louis Dreyfus bought across the board. Commission house buy stops were triggered at $170 then $170.50 in March and May. Those contracts ended up $1.80 at $170.80 and $170.50, respectively.
February western barley finished up $1.30 at $140 on commercial and commission house buying despite CBOT corn. About 200 Feb-Mar spread at $0.50. Volume was 1,580 lots.
Peas and oats did not trade.
(Values in Canadian dollars/tonne except peas, oats).
